subject: Access controls & support access follow-up / FinTrust discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@fintrust.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Access controls & support access follow-up / FinTrust discovery

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through FinTrust's production use case. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps around access controls and support access, per your ask: 

1) PII classification & data residency
- Redwood stores customer-provided prompts and outputs only when configured (default: no persistent storage for prompts). For customers that enable logs, we support region-specific storage (US, EU).

2) RBAC & least-privilege
- Our product supports role-based access with fine-grained permissions at the organization, project, and route level. Admin roles can manage keys and rollout policies; developer roles can create routes and view usage; support roles are scoped to session-level debugging only when explicitly authorized.

3) Support access & break-glass
- Standard support access is time-limited and audited. We provide break-glass procedures for escalations: customer triggers, short-lived access tokens, mandatory two-person approval for non-revocable access, and post-event audit logs.

4) Logging & retention
- Configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days) with encrypted-at-rest logs and support for customer-managed KMS for encryption keys.

Attachments: I included our security whitepaper and the SOC 2 report, plus a simple RBAC diagram for reference.

Proposed next steps:
- Can we schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your security team next week (Vivek from our infra team will join)?
- If you can share any specific policy templates (e.g., least-privilege checklist), we’ll map Redwood controls to them ahead of the call.

If this matches what you were hoping to see, I’ll set up the calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- redwood-security-whitepaper.pdf (PDF, 5 pages)
- SOC2-report-2026.pdf (PDF, executive summary stub)
- rbac-diagram.png (PNG, 1 file)

From: Alice Johnson <alice@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@fintrust.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T18:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls & support access follow-up / FinTrust discovery

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap and the docs. A few clarifying questions from our InfoSec team: 

- Break-glass: can you confirm whether break-glass access requires customer-initiated approval (e.g., a ticket in our system) or if Redwood can initiate with post-facto notification? We prefer customer-initiated gating for most escalations.

- Support access auditability: can we get daily exports of support session logs (id, start/end, operator, actions taken)? Also would prefer S3-compatible exports into our own bucket if possible.

- RBAC controls: do the permissions map to SAML groups or SCIM provisioning? We’d like to avoid manual role assignment where possible.

Happy to do the deep-dive — can we aim for Tue 11am PT next week? Ben and I will bring our security engineer.

Thanks,
Alice
Director, Cloud Security | FinTrust
alice@fintrust.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@fintrust.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T19:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls & support access follow-up / FinTrust discovery

Hi Alice —

Great questions — see answers inline below. I'm pulling Priyom and Vivek in to help with SCIM/exports.

- Break-glass: Our standard is customer-initiated gating for elevated access. For time-critical incidents we have an emergency workflow where Redwood can request break-glass, but it requires two internal approvers and we send immediate customer notification; if you prefer we can disable Redwood-initiated requests for your org.

- Support access auditability: Yes — we can provide daily log exports, and we support exporting session logs to an S3-compatible bucket you control. We’ll include the session id, operator id, timestamps, and a summary of actions.

- SCIM/SAML: We support SCIM provisioning for group sync and role mapping; SAML for SSO. SCIM allows you to map external groups to Redwood roles (e.g., security-team -> admin-readonly).

Next steps: I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 2027-05-11 11:00 AM PT with a short agenda (break-glass demo, SCIM mapping, export walkthrough). Priyom will prepare sample SCIM mappings and Vivek will demo the break-glass audit trail.

If you have any internal docs to share (least-privilege checklist or support access policy), please drop them in the Drive link and we’ll prepare a mapping doc beforehand.

Thanks,
Marissa
